## Computational biology, epigenomics and FAIR research data

::: {.affil}
PhD Researcher in Computational Biology & Pharmacoepigenomics, **University of Bradford**<br>
Lead Data Stewardship Trainer, **ELIXIR-UK**
:::

I build reproducible workflows for population epigenomics and teach researchers how to
manage data well. My doctoral work develops a cross-array framework for longitudinal
DNA methylation studies, applied to treatment-resistant schizophrenia in patients on
clozapine. Alongside the research I lead data stewardship training for ELIXIR-UK,
delivering around 30 hands-on workshops a year.

## What I work on

::: {.card-grid}
::: {}
#### Cross-array DNA methylation

Harmonising Illumina 450K and EPIC data so that longitudinal cohorts sampled years apart
can be analysed as one study, without the array generation driving the signal.
:::

::: {}
#### Pharmacoepigenomics

Methylation and pharmacogenomic markers of clozapine response in treatment-resistant
schizophrenia, and what array data can and cannot tell you about drug metabolism.
:::

::: {}
#### Reproducible workflows

Nextflow DSL2 and Galaxy tool suites, containerised and documented, so that an analysis
can be rerun years later by someone who did not write it.
:::

::: {}
#### FAIR data and training

Data stewardship curricula, Galaxy Training Network tutorials and train-the-trainer
programmes across European ELIXIR Nodes.
:::
:::
